question.text: A boy weighing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> eat some bananas. The energy content of the bananas is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi></math>. If the boy uses all of this energy to jump upwards from the ground, then the height up to which his centre of mass will rise is [mechanical equivalent of heat = <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cal</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Energy used by the boy is

E=1000×4.2 J

⇒4200=50×10×h

⇒h=8.4 m
